the persistence of IgM and IgM antibodies after vaccination is dependent on the ratio of these antibodies.
the IgM-to-Ign antibody ratio at 2 weeks postvaccination is an indicator for the long-term persistence of both IgG and IgM antibodies.
the IgM-to-Ign antibody ratio at 1 month postvaccination is an indicator for the long-term persistence of both IgG and IgM antibodies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the persistence of IgM and IgA antibodies in the serum of adults who were vaccinated with a combined group A and group c polysaccharide meningococcal vaccine.
the antibody response after vaccination with a meningococcal polysaccharide group A and group c vaccine.
the persistence of the antibody response to a combined meningococal A and C polysaccharid vaccine in adults.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the persistence of IgM antibodies was not related to the persistence of IgG antibodies.
a combined meningococcus group A and group c polysaccharide vaccination is effective and that it induces an immune response that is associated with the persistence of the antibody response.
the IgM-to-Ign ratio 14 days post vaccination can be used to predict the IgG persistence for 3 years.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the persistence of both polysaccharide-specific IgM and IgA antibodies in the blood of adults after vaccination with meningococcal polysaccharide vaccines is dependent on the ratio between these antibodies at 14 days after vaccination.
the IgM-to-Ign antibody ratio at 2 weeks after vaccination can be used as a predictor for the persistence of IgM and IgC antibody responses in adults for up to 3 years.
the IgM-to-Ign antibody ratio at 3 months after vaccination can be used to predict the persistence of IgM and IgM antibodies for the next 3.5 years.

IgM and Ig G antibody levels against the meningococcal polysaccharides A and C are positively related at 14 days and 3 years postvaccination.
